title: SET v1.8: a machine-checked mathematical framework with two registered, falsifiable predictions
description:
A body of mathematical work built from a single postulated object, the horn torus, whose radial metric is exactly the Fisher information metric of a Bernoulli variable, plus one experimental calibrant (N = 19,776, from the baryon-to-photon ratio) and an explicitly listed assumption ledger. The record derives a large set of physical quantities, labeled postdictions throughout, and a dark-matter candidate (derivation chain 31, status CANDIDATE, resting on the named two-clause postulate P-RING and, in its quantized sector, the named conditional Q-LAW).

The deposit's evidential exposure lives in two predictions registered on August 11, 2026, each with an explicit kill condition and no retreat clause. P6: the cosmological dark-matter-to-baryon density ratio converges to exactly 2pi - 1 = 5.2832 with zero adjustable parameters (CANDIDATE carrier on internally proven geometry; killed by a greater-than-3-sigma exclusion). P7: dark matter couples to ordinary matter at the proton's gravitational fine-structure constant and no stronger, so every direct-detection experiment stays empty at every mass in every channel (killed by any confirmed non-gravitational dark-matter signal). The originally cited decisive instrument for P6, CMB-S4, was cancelled by DOE and NSF on July 9, 2025; the successor experiment clock is recorded in the workbook and the pre-registration text.

Contents: the unified master state document, the master workbook (derivation chains 1-32, equations E1-E117, predictions register, assumption ledger, superseded register), the verification suite (94 machine checks, zero failures at issue), and nine supporting numeric scripts. Every claim labeled PROVEN carries a machine-executed check or a separately audited proof; the suite runs in minutes on commodity hardware with the pinned dependencies. The checks establish internal mathematical correctness only; the registered predictions are the framework's contact with measurement.

Code is MIT licensed; documents are CC BY 4.0.
